newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian VTM monopoly damages claim rejected.
newsitem.headline: Belgian VTM monopoly damages claim rejected.

text.p: Belgium's regional government of Flanders said on Thursday it would reject any claim in damages by the Belgian VTM commercial TV channel if, as expected, it loses its TV advertising monopoly.

"If the European Commission declares us in default today, we'll have to lift the monopoly...and adjust our laws. So I don't really see how there could be a claim for damages," Flemish Economic Affairs and Media minister Eric Van Rompuy told Belgian BRTN radio.
VTM said on Wednesday it would claim 15 to 20 billion francs ($420-560 million) in damages from the Flemish regional government if it lost its advertising monopoly.
The European Commission is expected to tell Belgium later on Thursday it must scrap the advertising monopoly granted to VTM or face legal action.

In 1989 VTM was given an 18-year advertising monopoly for Dutch-speaking Flanders, in northern Belgium, which has been attacked by rival channel VT4 owned by Nasdaq-listed TV group Scandinavian Broadcasting System (SBS).
VT4 has been forced to set up headquarters in London to circumvent VTM's monopoly and to be able to broadcast to Flanders.
The channel started operations in February 1995 despite the opposition of the Flemish regional government and took the issue to the Commission the same year.
